items.answer: Immersion is the objective, quantifiable degree to which a virtual reality system projects stimuli onto the sensory receptors of users in an extensive, matching, surrounding, vivid, interactive, and plot-informing way.

Virtual reality (VR) is an artificial environment experienced through sensory stimuli provided by a computer, in which a person's actions partially determine what happens and which replaces the user's sense of reality without requiring the physical existence of objects or places.

Virtual environment is a non-real, computer-generated graphical representation of a real or imaginary world, populated with artificial objects, that is experienced through computer-generated sensory stimuli.

A virtual reality system is a system that presents a computer-generated artificial environment, provides computer-generated sensory stimuli for an immersive experience, and lets the user's actions partially determine what happens in it.

questions.question: What is the main objective of a virtual reality system?
options: Letting a user perceive suitable sensory stimuli as a human-factor issue
Letting a user experience an artificial environment through computer-provided sensory stimuli
Letting a user distinguish real-world sensory stimuli from computer-provided sensory stimuli
Letting a user generate suitable sensory stimuli for an artificial environment
questions.explanation: A virtual reality system aims to let a user experience an artificial environment through sensory stimuli supplied by the computer. Generating stimuli is the technological issue, not the system's objective, and distinguishing virtual stimuli from real ones is not the stated aim.

questions.question: Why is perceiving virtual-reality stimuli suitably treated as a psychological human-factor issue?
options: Technology does not address it, and it is likely to differ between users
Technology makes it indistinguishable from real stimuli, and it is likely to differ between users
Technology projects it onto sensory receptors, and it is likely to be the same for all users
Technology generates it suitably, and it is likely to differ between users
questions.explanation: The psychological issue is how users perceive stimuli suitably; it is a human-factor concern that technology does not solve and that can vary from person to person. Generating or projecting stimuli belongs to the technological side, not the reason this issue is psychological.

questions.question: What two major concerns arise from the technological and psychological issues in virtual reality?
options: Extensiveness and interactivity
Immersion and presence
Sight and sound
Technology and psychology
questions.explanation: The technological and psychological issues of virtual reality give rise to the major concerns of immersion and presence. Technology and psychology are the issues behind the concerns, while extensiveness and interactivity are qualities of immersion, and sight and sound are only two sensory modalities.

data.text: A VR system aims to let a user experience an artificial environment through computer-provided stimuli for all sensory organs. The issues involved are technological in generating suitable stimuli and psychological in perceiving them, with the latter a human-factor issue that likely varies between users. These issues give rise to the recurring VR concerns of immersion and presence.
points: A VR system aims to let a user experience an artificial environment through computer-provided stimuli for all sensory organs.
VR broadly has two major issues: technological generation of suitable stimuli and psychological perception of them.
These technological and psychological VR issues give rise to the major concerns of immersion and presence.

questions.question: In Slater and Wilbur's definition, immersion is an objective degree describing what?
options: The projection of stimuli
The perception of stimuli
The control of stimuli
The understanding of stimuli
questions.explanation: Immersion is defined by how a VR system and application project stimuli onto users' sensory receptors. Perception, understanding, and control are not the defining objective property.

questions.question: When a user's physical movement is immediately reflected in the virtual world, which quality of immersion is shown?
options: The vivid quality
The surrounding quality
The matching quality
The plot-informing quality
questions.explanation: Matching refers to congruence between the user's physical movement and movement in the virtual world. Surrounding concerns panoramic coverage, vividness concerns sensory detail, and plot-informing concerns story understanding.

questions.question: A user can make changes, receive responses from virtual entities, and influence future events. Which quality of immersion does this describe?
options: The surrounding quality
The interactive quality
The matching quality
The vivid quality
questions.explanation: Interactivity is the user's capability to affect the virtual world and receive responses, not merely observe one-way feedback. Matching, surrounding, and vividness concern different aspects of immersion.

questions.question: In VR, which of these is the psychological concern rather than the technological one?
options: The immersion concern
The presence concern
The extensiveness concern
The vividness concern
questions.explanation: Immersion is the technological issue, while presence is the psychological issue. Vividness and extensiveness are qualities of immersion, not the separate psychological concern.

data.text: VR immersion is defined as the objective degree to which a system projects stimuli onto users' senses. Its six qualities describe that projection in terms of sensory range, movement congruence, panoramism, sensory energy, user influence, and story understandability. These qualities separate immersion, a technological system property, from presence, a psychological issue.
points: Slater and Wilbur define VR immersion as objective stimulus projection that is extensive, matching, surrounding, vivid, interactive, plot-informing.
Extensive, matching, surrounding, and vivid immersion mean sensory breadth, movement match, panoramic cues, and sensory energy.
Interactive and plot-informing immersion mean user influence and an understandable, predictable story.
In VR, immersion is the technological issue, while presence is the psychological issue.

questions.question: What characterizes presence as a psychological state?
options: Part of the perception fails to accurately acknowledge the role of the computer in the experience
Part of the perception fails to accurately acknowledge the role of the technology in the experience
Part of the perception fails to accurately acknowledge the role of the immersion in the experience
Part of the perception accurately acknowledges the role of the technology in the experience
questions.explanation: Presence is a psychological state in which part of the perception fails to accurately acknowledge the role of the technology in the experience. The tempting wrong options either reverse that failure or substitute another term, but the definition specifically concerns the technology’s role.

questions.question: In presence, what does the user perceive computer-generated stimuli as coming from?
options: The sensory organs
The real world
The system
The virtual world
questions.explanation: In presence, the user cannot distinguish computer-generated stimuli from real-world stimuli, so the stimuli are experienced as coming from the real world. The virtual world, the system, or the sensory organs are not the attributed source.

questions.question: What does perfect presence mean?
options: Failing to perceive the immersive qualities in the virtual world
Failing to distinguish the virtual world from the technological world
Failing to distinguish the virtual world from the real world
Failing to acknowledge the technology in the virtual world
questions.explanation: Perfect presence is specifically the inability to distinguish the virtual world from the real world. Failing to acknowledge technology or failing to perceive immersive qualities describes related aspects of presence, but not the specific criterion for perfect presence.

data.text: Presence is the psychological side of an immersive experience: it is a subjective state in which the user perceives the generated experience without accurately acknowledging the technology's role. When computer-generated stimuli are indistinguishable from real-world stimuli, the user perceives them as coming from the real world rather than from a computer. Perfect presence is the state in which the virtual world and the real world cannot be distinguished.
points: Presence is the subjective psychological state in which a user perceives the generated immersive qualities without accurately acknowledging technology's role.
In presence, computer-generated stimuli stimulate the senses and are perceived as real because they cannot be distinguished from real-world stimuli.
Perfect presence is the inability to distinguish the virtual world from the real world.

questions.question: Which option best distinguishes presence from immersion in a VR system?
options: Presence is a measured sensory range in the user, while immersion is a real-time feedback condition in the system
Presence is a subjective state in the user, while immersion is an objective property of the system
Presence is a feeling of control in the user, while immersion is a safe real-world boundary in the system
Presence is an objective property of the system, while immersion is a subjective state in the user
questions.explanation: Presence is the user's psychological sense of being in the virtual environment, whereas immersion describes what the system can objectively provide and measure. A swapped or mixed-up option confuses the side on which each concept belongs.

questions.question: How does immersion influence a user's sense of presence?
options: It can be equated with the user's subjective sense of presence
It can ensure a high degree of presence for a motivated user's subjective sense of presence
It can aid presence without ensuring presence
It can replace the user's subjective experience for presence
questions.explanation: Immersion can support or help produce presence, but presence also depends on the user's subjective experience, so high immersion raises the potential for presence rather than guaranteeing it.

questions.question: Why does creating a high degree of presence require a high degree of immersion?
options: Because the goal is to make users unable to distinguish the real world from the virtual world
Because the goal is to make the user's subjective state objective for the virtual world
Because the goal is to make user actions influence future events in the surrounding virtual world
Because the goal is to make the system's sensory range measurable for the virtual world
questions.explanation: The overall goal of a VR system is a high degree of presence, meaning users feel really in the virtual world and cannot distinguish it from the real one; achieving that goal systemically requires high immersion. The other options describe related system qualities, not the presence goal.

data.text: Immersion and presence are distinct qualities of a VR experience, one objective and one subjective. Immersion describes what a VR system can provide and can be measured, while presence is the user's psychological sense of being in the virtual environment. Presence can depend on both subjective experience and the system's immersion, so greater immersion raises and lesser immersion lowers the potential for presence without ensuring it. The overall goal of a VR system is to create high presence, which requires the system to provide high immersion, a systemic issue.
points: Immersion is an objective, quantifiable description of what a VR system can provide.
Presence is a user's subjective, hard-to-measure psychological sense of being in the virtual environment.
Presence can depend on subjective experience and immersion; greater immersion raises and lesser lowers presence potential, not guaranteeing it.
A VR system's overall goal of high presence requires high immersion, a systemic issue.

questions.question: What role does an early virtual-reality paper play in establishing XR vocabulary?
options: It supplies terms and definitions for immersive technology and gaming
It supplies terms and definitions for immersion and presence
It supplies terms and definitions for healthcare and education
It supplies terms and definitions for HMDs and virtual environments
questions.explanation: The paper is a source for the terms and definitions of immersion and presence. It is not the cited source for hardware or application-domain terminology.

data.text: Slater and Wilbur's 1997 paper is an early source in the area of VR immersion and presence. It is one of the references from which the terms and definitions of immersion and presence are taken.
points: Slater and Wilbur's 1997 paper is an early reference for VR immersion and presence definitions.

questions.question: Why are immersion and presence treated as different concerns in virtual reality?
questions.reference_answer: The two major issues in virtual reality are technological, about generating suitable sensory stimuli, and psychological, about how a user perceives those stimuli. These issues give rise to immersion and presence as central concerns. Immersion corresponds to the technological issue, while presence corresponds to the psychological issue.

questions.question: How can a virtual reality system provide a high degree of immersion without guaranteeing a high degree of presence?
questions.reference_answer: A virtual reality system can provide a high degree of immersion without guaranteeing a high degree of presence, because immersion is an objective and quantifiable description of what a system can provide or does provide, while presence is a subjective psychological state inside the user's mind. Immersion can aid an enhanced perception of presence and is capable of producing presence, but it does not ensure presence; greater immersion increases the potential for presence.

questions.question: How do display resolution and field of view contribute to different qualities of immersion in a virtual reality system?
questions.reference_answer: Display resolution affects vividness, because higher resolution increases the energy stimulated in a sensory modality and improves visual perception. Field of view affects surrounding, because a wider field of view makes the visual cues more panoramic than a narrow field of view.
